div.l: His resoıı̄uns he spak / ful solempnely
Sownyng alway / thencrees of his wynnyng
He wolde the see / were kept for any thing
By twixt Middyl borowhe / and Orewelle
Weel cowde he in eschaunge / sheedys selle
This worthy man̄ ful wel / his wit beset
Ther woste no wyhgt / that he was in det
So estatlych was he / of his gouernaıı̄unce
With his bargayns / and with his chevysaıı̄unce
For sothe he was / a worthi man̄ with alle
But soth to telle / I not how mēn hym calle
A Clerk of Oxenford A Clerke ther was / of Oxynforde also
That vnto logyk / hadde longe I go
As leene was his hors / as is a rake
And he was nat ryht fate I vndertake
But loked holowe / and therto sobirly
Wol thredbare was / his ovirmest courtepy
For he ne hadde get hym / yet no benefys
Ne was so wordlich for to haue offys
For hym was lever / to have / at his beddys hed
Twenty bokes / clad in blak and reed
Of Aristotele / and his philosophie
Than̄ robys riche / other fethele or Sawterye
But al bi that / he was a philozophre
Yet hadde he but litel / gold in cofre
But alle that he myhte / of his frendys hente
On bokes and on lernyng / he it spente
And besyly gan / for the sowles preye
Of hem that yaf / wherwith to scoleye
Of studye toke he / most cure and heed
Nowt on word spak he / more than was need
And that was seyde in forme / and reuerence
And short and quyk / and ful of high sentence
